relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-property
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, same union-of-grants semantics minted in access-control-how-verify-access.json, corroborated here with this page's own quote and its own reasoning (repeated invocation across documents)
relations.evidence: The effects of all access calls by all active documents are effectively combined in a union, so if _any_ document grants a user access to a channel, that user has access to the channel.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd

relations.evidence: Routing changes have no effect until the document is actually saved in the database, so if the sync function first calls `channel()` or `access()`, but then rejects the update, the channel and access changes will not occur.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-wildcard
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted relation, established in access-control-concepts.json; this page's own reference-level quote adds a fuller mechanistic reason (requireAccess only recognizes explicit named-channel grants)
relations.evidence:
Note that `requireAccess()` will only recognize grants made explicitly using a channel name (not by a wildcard).

So, if a user was granted access using only the [all channels wildcard](../channels.md#lbl-all-channels)\] (`*`), then `requireAccess('anychannelname')'` will fail because the user wasn't granted access to that channel (only to the `*` channel).

notable_absence.finding: This page restates, with its own quote, the fail-silent role() behavior already flagged in access-control-how-assign-users-to-roles.json's notable_absence: 'Nonexistent roles don't cause an error, but have no effect on the user's access privileges.' It adds one genuinely new nuance not previously captured: role assignments can be made retroactively consistent-with-future-state - 'You can create roles retrospectively. As soon as a role is created, any pre-existing references to it take effect.' In other words, a role() call referencing a not-yet-created role is not just silently ignored once, it is silently RE-EVALUATED once the role comes into existence, and prior document revisions' role() calls will then take effect. This is a deferred-activation behavior with no described re-evaluation trigger (it is unclear from this page alone whether this happens on the next sync-function invocation for that document, or on some other schedule) and no analogue anywhere else in the corpus's privilege/role models, which are checked once, synchronously, at grant or operation time.

cross_component_finding: access()'s documented performance warning is worth surfacing: 'If you invoke the `access()` function multiple times to grant the same user access to the same channel, you could see negative performance effects, such as large fetches or request timeouts.' Combined with the union-of-all-active-documents semantics ('The effects of all access calls by all active documents are effectively combined in a union'), this means SGW's channel-grant model has a per-document, per-invocation COST that a hand-authored sync function can accidentally multiply across every document revision ever processed - there is no equivalent performance warning attached to any operation in server/'s RBAC or Capella's role model in the corpus so far, since granting a privilege or role there is a single, one-time administrative action rather than logic that re-runs on every document write.
cross_product_finding: The 'Star Channel' cross-reference in this page's duplicated 'Default Sync Function Examples' section repeats the same malformed link target already flagged on auto-purge-channel-access-revocation.json: '[Star Channel](#2.7@sync-gateway-channels.adoc#star-channel)'. Its appearing verbatim, byte-for-byte, on two structurally unrelated pages (an API reference page and a revocation-behavior conceptual page) confirms this is a repeated build/authoring artifact - likely a single AsciiDoc include fragment reused on both source pages - rather than an isolated typo, strengthening the case for raising it as a docs-issue in reconciliation.
